sn44.8:1.1: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
sn44.8:1.2: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn44.8:1.3: “How is it, Master Gotama, is the world eternal?”…
sn44.8:2.1: “What, Master Gotama, is the cause and reason why, when wanderers of other sects are asked such questions, they give such answers as:
sn44.8:2.3: or ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’
sn44.8:2.4: And what is the cause and reason why, when Master Gotama is asked such questions, he does not give such answers?”
sn44.8:3.1: “Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form.
sn44.8:3.5: consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness.
sn44.8:3.6: Therefore, when the wanderers of other sects are asked such questions, they give such answers as:
sn44.8:3.8: or ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’
sn44.8:3.9: But, Vaccha, the Tathagata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not regard form as self …
sn44.8:3.14: Therefore, when the Tathagata is asked such questions, he does not give such answers.”
sn44.8:4.1: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and approached the Venerable Mahamoggallana. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Mahamoggallana … and said to him:
sn44.8:4.3: “How is it, Master Moggallana, is the world eternal?”
sn44.8:4.6: “Vaccha, the Blessed One has not declared this either:
sn44.8:4.7: ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”
sn44.8:5.1: “What, Master Moggallana, is the cause and reason why, when wanderers of other sects are asked such questions, they give such answers as:
sn44.8:5.3: or ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?
sn44.8:5.4: And what is the cause and reason why when the ascetic Gotama is asked such questions,
sn44.8:5.6: he does not give such answers?”
sn44.8:6.1: “Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self … or self as in consciousness.
sn44.8:6.6: Therefore, when the wanderers of other sects are asked such questions, they give such answers as:
sn44.8:6.8: or ‘The Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’
sn44.8:6.9: But, Vaccha, the Tathagata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not regard form as self …
sn44.8:6.14: Therefore, when the Tathagata is asked such questions, he does not give such answers.”
sn44.8:7.1: “It is wonderful, Master Moggallana! It is amazing, Master Moggallana!
sn44.8:7.2: How the meaning and the phrasing of both teacher and disciple coincide and agree with each other and do not diverge, that is, in regard to the chief matter.
sn44.8:7.3: Just now, Master Moggallana, I approached the ascetic Gotama and asked him about this matter.
sn44.8:7.4: The ascetic Gotama explained this matter to me in exactly the same terms and phrases that Master Moggallana used.
sn44.8:7.5: It is wonderful, Master Moggallana! It is amazing, Master Moggallana!
sn44.8:7.6: How the meaning and the phrasing of both teacher and disciple coincide and agree with each other and do not diverge, that is, in regard to the chief matter.”
